A NotFoundError is thrown when looking up a project, its board, or an issue's comment thread.

Writes to projects and their issues, comments, or status also throw NotFoundError. Listings silently omit these items. Search is out of scope. I need to find all service functions touching projects, issues, or comments.

Project membership must be fetched from the database on every check rather than cached. Lead changes are already reflected because the lead lives on the project object. I will examine the comment service, issue list repository, project list repository, and any other services that read issues or projects.

Activity, attachments, labels, and notifications are excluded from the NotFoundError scope. The explicit list is authoritative over the general rule. I will cover every service entry point that exposes project contents.

I will also inspect attachment, label, activity, and search services, plus API routes that bypass the service layer. Existing tests should reveal coverage patterns. I need to decide whether filtering belongs in the repository or service layer. Listings must silently omit hidden items, and total counts should reflect only what the actor can see.

Filtering after pagination would corrupt page sizes and totals. The repository query must handle visibility checks directly, since canViewProject is asynchronous and per-project. Listing many projects efficiently requires an efficient query strategy.

I need to understand the full scope of writes and reads.

Reviewing issue service REST endpoints, attachments, and activity routes. The `canViewProject` design checks visibility, platform staff status, admin or owner roles, lead assignment, and project membership.

Considering whether admin or owner roles should be scoped to the same organization. The actor is already bound to one org, so cross-tenant access is likely blocked by assertOrgScope before visibility checks run. Private projects must return NotFoundError rather than a permission error.

The `canViewProject` function should return false when the actor and project belong to different organizations. Even platform staff must be scoped to the same orgId, so cross-organization access is not permitted.

Non-private projects are unaffected by the visibility check. The function returns true for org and public projects regardless of organization. Private projects are restricted to admins, owners, platform staff, leads, and members.

Platform staff bypasses will apply unconditionally, while admin and owner checks remain scoped to the same organization.

The `isProjectMember` check filters by the project's organization ID, so a user may match membership even if the actor belongs to a different organization. This is acceptable because service methods already enforce cross-tenant access through `assertOrgScope`.

The `hasRoleAtLeast` helper is the sanctioned way to check admin or owner status. This avoids direct role branching and aligns with the existing permissions pattern.

I need to understand pagination to filter lists correctly.

Filtering after pagination would break total counts. Visibility checks must move into the repository layer. Jobs call repositories directly, so the filter needs to be optional.

The service layer can compute an exclude set of private project IDs for the actor and pass them to the repository. Admins and staff would have no exclusions. Other users would lose access to private projects where they are not lead or member. A repository helper or SQL predicate could identify those hidden IDs.

The SQL visibility predicate will include public projects, projects where the actor is lead, admin or staff status, and membership in project_members. Issues will be restricted to visible projects. If a user filters by a private project they cannot see, the list returns empty with zero total. Individual lookups of hidden issues still throw NotFound.

Visibility checks must run before permission assertions. Otherwise a viewer who cannot see a project would receive a PermissionDeniedError instead of the required NotFoundError.

The ordering of visibility and permission checks does not matter for regular members. A member who is not on a private project passes the read assertion but still gets NotFound when visibility blocks access. The same holds for viewers who are also project members.

Visibility checks must precede permission assertions for writes. Members have project:update rights by role, so a member on the wrong private project would otherwise succeed without the visibility gate. Viewers attempting updates hit PermissionDeniedError from assertCan before visibility is reached.

A lead who is also a viewer can see a private project but cannot archive it. A member with viewer role can see the project but cannot create issues. Both cases correctly return PermissionDeniedError after the visibility check.

The implementation plan adds a `canViewProject` helper and an `assertCanViewProject` helper that throws NotFoundError. This helper will be called in all specified service methods before permission assertions and before mutations.

I am auditing all exported functions across issue-service, comment-service, and the activity feed to find every path that exposes project contents. The org-wide issue list is listIssues.
